script.name: Nephrotic syndrome

epidemiology.who: Children, usually from minimal change disease, and adults, most often from membranous nephropathy, FSGS or diabetic kidney disease

script.pathophysiology: Injury to the glomerular filtration barrier (the podocytes) lets large amounts of protein leak into the urine, causing low serum albumin, edema and a compensatory rise in hepatic lipoprotein synthesis. Urinary loss of anticoagulant proteins makes patients hypercoagulable.

timeline.course: Minimal change disease often remits with steroids; other causes may progress to chronic kidney disease

history: swelling around the eyes and legs
labs: fatty casts and oval fat bodies in the urine

confirmatory_tests: kidney biopsy to find the cause in adults
criteria: proteinuria above 3.5 g/day with hypoalbuminemia and edema; hyperlipidemia is common

first_line: ACE inhibitor or ARB to reduce proteinuria
loop diuretics and salt restriction for edema

complications: deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

confused_with.how_to_tell_apart: Nephritic syndrome has hematuria with red blood cell casts, hypertension and a rising creatinine, with proteinuria usually below 3.5 g/day; nephrotic syndrome has heavy proteinuria above 3.5 g/day with a bland sediment.

pearls: Urinary loss of antithrombin III makes nephrotic patients hypercoagulable; renal vein thrombosis is classic with membranous nephropathy.

sources.title: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases
